artistStatement: A grouping of two or more Waves installed in or near water highlights the rippling effect of the grouping. The water and grouping complement each other as they live and breath with the wind.

The Double Spinner design is a favorite as one piece and as you add more of varying heights it only amplifies the flowering illusion with even greater intensity. When displayed in a linear fashion along a border or walkway it presents a journey of experience from one end to the other.
The Twister Oval’s expanding flow opens up space for pieces like the Double Dancer or Single Helix Oval to be nestled close and create mesmerizing interplay of movement.

From the beginning Lyman envisioned having the Element Air, Element Earth, Element Fire, and Element Water together as a grouping. Just as in life, all the elements together provides a sense of complementary completeness.

An array of multiple designs and movements that radiates from a strong tall center out to eye level height can be an incredibly engaging interactive display. The display’s movement mimics the shape with smooth slower movements in the center that speed up as you flow to the displays outer edges.
Displaying a few Lotus in water feels like a natural placement. The pieces can bring the water to life. This grouping was displayed at the Dallas Arboretum for about a year.

The Gemini’s distinct leaf-like cup shape inspired Lyman to center a grouping of them with the same cup on the Twister shape, called the Twister Leaf. The grouping is bordered by the Sail design, which seemlessly brings the grouping to and end.

The Twister Oval is often a center piece because of its strong presence and mesmerizing fluid motion. When put together with others of the same design the pieces magnify the fluid spiral motion creating a sense of awe. This grouping is on display in Sugarland, TX.

The Windflower, Agave, Double Spinner, Tulip, Desert Flame, and Sail can accentuate home adding their flower like qualities like a well manicured planter. Their interactive nature adds a playful energy to the space they fill. Displayed temporarily at the Morris Arboretum.

The Double Helix Horizontal was one of Lyman’s original designs. Available in varying sizes the peaceful turn is amplified when grouped with more. The groupings are mesmorizing whether placed in a line or scattered in a grouping to add depth and height.

Like the shoots of a larger tree, the Sails positioned through the Double Helix Sails in this display
mimick the replenishing of a forest. This grouping was displayed at the Dallas Arboretum.
The Double Spinner supported by Twister Ovals creates a dymanic on Old Highway 91 in Southern Utah that is stunning to watch from every angle.

The Mirinda III is a design that welcomes designs of all shapes to join it. Its sloping nature to the
center allows it to tuck into the twists of other pieces, like can be seen when next to the Helix Vertical. Placing it next to a Desert Lily demonstrates its ability to fill in the space below

The Double Helix Vertical and Double Helix Horizontal share a common shape but are distinct in
feel. Add a Double Spinner inbetween, which nestles perfectly with their shape and it brings your focus to the center and the distinctness of the shapes add character to the periphery.

You can’t help but follow the three Bean Poles upward along their cascading ovals as the spiral
upward. This display was created with children in mind for the entrance to the Children’s Garden at the Dallas Arboretum. The Single Helix Ovals add to the joy by moving the opposite way. This gives the display a sense
of spontaneaty not unlike that
of a child full of energy.
The triple Wave grouping is one of the Artist’s favorites. It seems to work regardless of how it is configured and its mesmerizing effects are seen from every angle it can be viewed.

This mirrored grouping created a welcome entrance through the hedge it adorned at the Dallas Arboretum in a year-long installation. The step-down slope of the display and contrast in shapes pulled people in time and time again.

The Agave is a playful piece representative of the agave plant. Add a little whimsicalness with the
Nebula or emphasize the plant basis with a Desert Lily and watch as either of these groupings captivate your attention.

Strategicly laid out to make the most from every angle well travelled this display in Lancaster, PA was one of Lyman’s largest. This is the Northwest display with an emphasis on the double helix design of the Double Helix Horizontal and Double Helix Sail. A Twister Oval Extra-Huge is the
focal point and reaches the highest.

Lyman’s counter-rotating pieces - with movement in opposing directions vertically - and tiered
pieces - with movement in opposing directions stacked horizontally - add dimension and excitement to any display. This display brings together the floral focused pieces of the Red Ginger, Lotus, and Double Spinner creating a vibrant display that
resembles the spirit of a fresh bloom.

Bringing a Tulip to any pairing will add a sense of energy to the piece it’s paired with. The Tulip
will spin as quickly as the wind while other designs will regulate the wind or even find its pulse.

Stainless has found a way to both call attention and somehow blend into the nature around it. This display places the Elements of the Universe as its centerpiece. However it is the Heart design that calls your attention to the display
that otherwise fits perfectly in its
plant filled scene. This display was
shown at the Dallas Arboretum for
about a year and was even more
dazzling at night.

The Bean Pole is a taller narrower shape than most of Lyman’s designs. With lower designs like
the Mirinda III, Tulip, and Desert Flame, it becomes like a flower stalk rising from the grouping. Pair with a design that is more midline, like the Single Helix Oval or Double Helix Horizontal - or both - and it becomes like the leader shoot of a plant extending above the others

The Garden of Ginger has the feel of flowers in full bloom and adding a couple of Red Ginger elements under the eves of the bloom embraces the feel of a plant full of life and growing. This display was shown at the Dallas Arboretum for about a year.
The Twister Oval’s feel changes just slightly with each size and nestling different sizes together brings dimensions and a new energy to each piece.

With the Nebula’s ability to pull you into the center of the piece and the Galaxy’s sense of vastness spreading out, this grouping balances both impressions with an engaging harmony. This display is on display in Merschel Park in North Carolina

This display provides a vision of scale and contrast. Each side a variation of a theme from being
centered with the Double Helix form of the Star Dancer Vertical and Double Helix Vertical to
the double cupped pieces of the Ponderosa and Double Dancer. The pattern continues until the
end where it is mirrored with two Tulips, the only time this display has more than one of the same
design.
The Tulip is a piece that can be used to line a hedge or walkway and add depth and energy to the space they fill. This grouping was displayed at the Dallas Arboretum for about a year.

The Weeping Willows drooping branches create an opportunity for the Windflower to flourish underneath.
This display will draw you in with the way the three move together.

The Spring is a piece that brings bold shapes together wtih delicate pieces in the center surrounded by space. Adding the Nautilus and Desert Flame to each side, both strong pieces in their own right, emphasizes the feel that Spring is
guarding its inner growth.

The Lotus is a piece that works well paired with the smaller version of itself. The simplicity of this grouping belies the depth of its effect. Each half of the pieces rotates a different direction than the other. The two are full of life in a peaceful relaxing way.

The Double Helix Sail’s sweeping flow gives it a delicate feel. That same shape gives way for
space that when filled with the Double Dancer adds a sense of protection. The movement mimics the visual sense with the long sweeps of the Double Helix Sail supported by the consistent rythm of the Double Dancer.
The Wave is a slender design that ripples as it turns. Placing a trio of Waves brings the pieces in and out of synchronicity in a captivating way. This trio is on display in Lehi, UT.

Pairing Double Spinners is a simple yet rewarding combination. The kaleidoscope effect is amplified
when seen two at a time. This pairing brings out the playfulness of the pieces.

When the Double Helix Sail is grouped with with the Sail, the grouping gives the impression
that the smaller Sails look up to the Double Helix form - aspiring to earn its symmetry. The playful interaction is reminiscent children looking up to their parents. Currently on display in Lehi, UT.

Pulling together the Mirinda III, Desert Lily, and Gaurdian Angel allows for a perfect framining
through a window or fill a space in your landscaping. While nearly equal in height, each has its own
personality that compliments the others around while each design displays its distinctness.

Bringing the Tulip and Mirinda III just under the Double Spinners span brings out an engaging
dynamic. From this display you can interpret the speed of the wind, the consistency of its direction and follow the suns ever changing position as it glistens through the Mirinda’s strips.
Another half to the display at Lancaster, PA, this grouping brings the Double Dancer form in with the Double Helix and keeps the Twister Oval as the focal point.
The Twister Oval’s feel changes just slightly with each size and nestling different sizes together brings dimensions and a new energy to each piece. This grouping is displayed at Lehi, UT.

Nestling a couple of Nebulas at the base of the Elements of the Universe broadens the feel of the galaxy it generates. The pieces pull you in from various angles bringing your attention to each element one-by-one.

This stunning stainless grouping was displayed in Black Rock City, NV at the Burning Man festival. The grouping brought together shapes in an engaging and playful way pulling people in day and night to dance and celebrate.
